conditions.default: The current skill with the plain triage prompt; detail reads follow the detail band.
conditions.full-read: The current skill with the same prompt plus a request to read every open issue in full, which the detail-read rule allows.

execution.comparison: Both conditions are with-skill runs of the current skill. Each scenario has a default case and a full-read case with the same fixture, overlay, and expected answer. Run every case on both agents, three runs per case, and compare the conditions within each agent.

gh_stand_in.stage: python3 stage_gh.py stage --run <run.json> --dest <new absolute staging dir> --tmpdir <run temp dir>
gh_stand_in.forms: The stand-in answers only the gh command forms that github-issue-triage's SKILL.md documents, with their exact --json field sets and --jq expressions, and refuses everything else with exit 1, no stdout, and a fixed stderr line.
gh_stand_in.note: stage_gh.py sits beside this file, outside files/, so prepare.py never copies it into a workspace. The fixture's bin/gh is the source of the staged copy; candidates reach gh only through the staged copy on PATH.

execution.decision_rule: Fixed before any run. A run matches when its recommended next issue equals expected.next, its current wave equals expected.current_wave as a set, and its next wave equals expected.next_wave as a set; a default run in addition names no parallel group that pairs an issue in expected.not_parallel_with_next with expected.next. A full-read run's parallel groups are recorded, not graded. Read scope never comes from the report or from output content; it comes from the arguments of reconciled ledger calls. Only the documented gh issue view form returns an issue's body and comments, so detail_issues lists the issues that successful calls of that form named. A default run whose detail_issues holds every open issue is graded but reported as band not exercised and not counted as detail-band evidence. A default run whose detail_issues holds an issue in read_scope.list_only is graded but reported as not exercising the list-only guard. A full-read run counts only when detail_issues holds every issue in read_scope.detail; otherwise, or when its calls do not reconcile one to one with the transcript, exclude it from the full-read count and rerun it once. Per case and agent, a counted default run that fails the rule is a detail-band regression only when a majority of that case's valid full-read runs for the same agent match the expected answer; otherwise, including when no full-read run is valid, report the case as inconclusive (suspected case defect). Byte totals are recorded, not gated.

recorded_fields.next: The issue the report recommends next.
recorded_fields.current_wave: The issues the report lists in the current wave.
recorded_fields.next_wave: The issues the report lists in the next wave.
recorded_fields.parallel_groups: The parallel groups and unverified issues the report names.
recorded_fields.detail_reads: The issues on the report's Detail reads line and its list-only issues, beside detail_issues from the collected ledger.
recorded_fields.gh_bytes: gh_bytes and gh_bytes_by_form from the collected ledger.

claude.policy: Both conditions get the same extra arguments plus --settings with the absolute path of claude_settings, resolved relative to this file, appended to the prepared launch_argv with the CLI's noninteractive flags and no permission-bypass flag. Each run gets a new, empty directory as the environment variable named in fresh_tmpdir.env, with a path short enough that <dir>/claude-<uid> stays within max_per_uid_path_bytes; a longer path makes the CLI fall back to the shared /tmp/claude-<uid>. Candidates may run commands inside the workspace under the OS sandbox in claude_settings: writes only to the workspace and the run's temp directory, no network, and no reads of ~/.dotfiles, ~/.claude, or ~/.agents. Edit and Write tools are not allowed. Before launch, run stage_gh.py stage with the run.json, a new absolute staging directory outside the workspace and the run's temp directory, and that temp directory, from the coordinator's environment. It resolves the prepared launch_argv's CLI to an absolute executable from the coordinator's PATH, before the fixed PATH applies, and rejects one in a directory the candidate can write; use the launch_argv it prints, with that absolute CLI, for the pre-run checks and the launch, and launch with the PATH and GH_SNAPSHOT_LOG it prints. That PATH is fixed, never inherited: the read-only staged bin, then /usr/bin, /bin, /usr/sbin, and /sbin, none of which the candidate can write, so neither candidate commands nor inherited hooks, which run outside the sandbox with the agent process's PATH, can resolve an executable the candidate wrote.
pre_run_checks: Every effective Claude settings source other than claude_settings (user, project, local, and managed) sets no sandbox key and no permissions.allow rule; record the result and do not start runs otherwise.
Inherited hooks run outside the sandbox: no effective hook command runs or sources a file in the workspace or the run's temp directory; record the hook commands and do not start runs otherwise.

In a throwaway workspace prepared and staged the same way, under the same settings and sandbox and the printed environment, with the printed absolute CLI: the CLI starts, command -v gh prints the staged stand-in, gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url,defaultBranchRef succeeds and appends a ledger line whose exe is the staged stand-in, gh auth status exits 1 with no stdout, and a write into the staging directory fails. Resolve every effective hook command's executable with that PATH, or take its absolute path: each lies outside the workspace, the run's temp directory, and the staging directory, or does not resolve and so runs nothing. Record the result and do not start runs otherwise.
post_run_checks: <dir>/claude-<uid> exists under the run's fresh temp directory, showing that the run's TMPDIR did not fall back to the shared temp root; exclude the run otherwise.

Before cleanup, run stage_gh.py collect with the run.json and a new evidence directory outside the workspace; within one deadline it opens the ledger without blocking or following symbolic links, accepts only a single-link regular file within its byte limit, validates every record, and keeps a copy. If it exits non-zero, exclude the run. Reconcile each ledger line with the transcript: every gh call in the transcript has a ledger line with the same arguments and exit status, every ledger line has such a transcript call, and every line's exe is the staged stand-in; exclude the run when any call is missing, extra, or cannot be matched one to one. The collector derives each record's form and issue from its arguments and exit status with the stand-in's command rules and fails on a record whose stored form or detail disagrees, so detail_issues comes from the reconciled arguments only. Record gh_bytes and gh_bytes_by_form as information, and detail_issues for grading.

Delete the run's workspace, temp directory, and staging directory, restoring write permission on the staging directory first, once its transcript, final answer, file hashes, and collected ledger are retained.

codex.policy: Both conditions insert exec after codex in the prepared launch_argv, keep its arguments, then append extra_args, one -c mcp_servers.<name>.enabled=false per MCP server found by the pre-run check, and --skip-git-repo-check --json -, with no --sandbox, approval-bypass, or hook-trust-bypass flag. The skill_eval permission profile lets commands write only to the workspace and the run's temp directory, blocks the network, and blocks reads of ~/.dotfiles, ~/.claude, ~/.agents, and Codex's installed skills and session transcripts. Commands that need more fail instead of asking, because the approval policy is never. Each run gets a new, empty directory as TMPDIR. apply_patch stays available, so the file-hash assertion catches an edit. Before launch, run stage_gh.py stage with the run.json, a new absolute staging directory outside the workspace and the run's temp directory, and that temp directory, from the coordinator's environment. It resolves the prepared launch_argv's CLI to an absolute executable from the coordinator's PATH, before the fixed PATH applies, and rejects one in a directory the candidate can write; use the launch_argv it prints, with that absolute CLI, for the pre-run checks and the launch, and launch with the PATH and GH_SNAPSHOT_LOG it prints. That PATH is fixed, never inherited: the read-only staged bin, then /usr/bin, /bin, /usr/sbin, and /sbin, none of which the candidate can write, so neither candidate commands nor inherited hooks, which run outside the sandbox with the agent process's PATH, can resolve an executable the candidate wrote.
pre_run_checks: List the MCP servers in the effective Codex config and disable each one for both conditions with -c mcp_servers.<name>.enabled=false; record the names.

From an empty scratch directory, run codex debug prompt-input with the same -c and --disable arguments before the subcommand: the permissions instructions show the denied reads, restricted network, and approval policy never, and the tool list has no browser, computer-use, web search, or MCP server tool; record the result and do not start runs otherwise.

Run codex sandbox -P skill_eval with the same -c arguments from that directory: a write there succeeds, a write outside it fails, a read of each denied path fails, and a network request fails; record the result and do not start runs otherwise.
Global instructions that Codex loads, such as ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, apply to both conditions; record their presence.

With codex sandbox -P skill_eval and the same -c arguments: in a throwaway workspace prepared and staged the same way, under the same settings and sandbox and the printed environment, with the printed absolute CLI: the CLI starts, command -v gh prints the staged stand-in, gh repo view --json nameWithOwner,url,defaultBranchRef succeeds and appends a ledger line whose exe is the staged stand-in, gh auth status exits 1 with no stdout, and a write into the staging directory fails. Hooks are off with --disable hooks; still resolve every configured hook command's executable with that PATH, or take its absolute path: each lies outside the workspace, the run's temp directory, and the staging directory, or does not resolve and so runs nothing. Record the result and do not start runs otherwise.
post_run_checks: The run's event stream shows the pinned model and no turn with a different model or effort; exclude the run otherwise.

Before cleanup, run stage_gh.py collect with the run.json and a new evidence directory outside the workspace; within one deadline it opens the ledger without blocking or following symbolic links, accepts only a single-link regular file within its byte limit, validates every record, and keeps a copy. If it exits non-zero, exclude the run. Reconcile each ledger line with the transcript: every gh call in the transcript has a ledger line with the same arguments and exit status, every ledger line has such a transcript call, and every line's exe is the staged stand-in; exclude the run when any call is missing, extra, or cannot be matched one to one. The collector derives each record's form and issue from its arguments and exit status with the stand-in's command rules and fails on a record whose stored form or detail disagrees, so detail_issues comes from the reconciled arguments only. Record gh_bytes and gh_bytes_by_form as information, and detail_issues for grading.

Delete the run's workspace, temp directory, and staging directory, restoring write permission on the staging directory first, once its transcript, final answer, file hashes, and collected ledger are retained.

known_constraints: The fixture has no .git directory, so git commands fail; the prompt states the git context.

The gh stand-in refuses every gh form the skill does not document, including other --json fields, other --jq expressions, short flags, and gh auth status; a candidate that varies a documented command gets exit 1 and no output.
The stand-in runs with /usr/bin/env python3 from the fixed PATH, so it stays compatible with the system Python 3.9.
execution.contamination: Exclude a run whose transcript reads or edits a file under .snapshot/ directly, runs a gh other than the staged stand-in, or reaches a repository or installed skill outside the workspace, another run's workspace or temp directory, the shared temp root, or the network, and rerun it once under the same conditions. Report a second contaminated run as missing coverage.

evals.name: dependent-text-raises-blocker
evals.prompt: Triage the open GitHub issues of this repository and recommend the next issue to handle. This copy has no git history: the branch is main, the worktree is clean, and there are no other worktrees. GitHub is reachable only through the gh command on PATH. Work directly in this session without subagents, leave the project files unedited, and report in the skill's output format.
evals.expected_output: The overview places #10 (export-v1 milestone) next and #11 (refactor) low. #12's title names it a follow-up of #11, so its placement needs a detail read. #12's body shows a crash that makes export to a file unusable, a bug blocking the core path, so re-placing #12 together with its native blocker moves #11 ahead of #10 as the foundation item that unblocks it.
assertions: The recommended next issue is #11
The current wave is exactly #10, #11, and #13, in any order
The next wave is exactly #12, in any order

Every gh command in the transcript has a matching line in the collected ledger, every ledger line has a transcript call, every line's exe is the staged stand-in, and the transcript reads or writes no file under .snapshot/ directly
The project files other than .snapshot/gh-calls.jsonl remain byte-identical to the initial fixture
